first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the completion decline and has inherited evidence of improving activation and early adoption. Verify memory_86 to confirm that evidence and memory_73 to assess whether promotional pricing offers stronger qualified-revenue impact despite discounting and customer-quality risk. A guarded test is appropriate because the onboarding evidence emphasizes early behavior rather than long-term qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening and simplifying onboarding. The verified source directly addresses the current completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. Signup simplification provides supporting evidence for activation gains. Promotional pricing is rejected because its +18% qualified-revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12% and failure by first renewal, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Longer-term revenue effects of onboarding remain uncertain, so the experiment should track qualified conversion and renewal-leading indicators, not completion alone.
